indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.initialization: let mut index = 0; block.resize_with(values.len(), || { let value = values[index]; index += 1; value });
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.hypothesis: Reserving once through resize_with rather than extending an iterator may remove per-element capacity-check overhead while retaining the final representation copy.
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.paired_order: Six alternating process pairs, extend first and indexed resize second; no agent-initiated build overlapped samples, host otherwise uncontrolled.
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.conclusion: Indexed resize median was about 34.4 ms versus 38.9 ms for extend in these samples, with overlapping ranges. This does not establish the cause or eliminate the previously observed raw-copy performance gap; the raw baseline was not rerun in this paired trial.
indexed_resize_with_then_copy_from_slice.disposition: Rejected as sufficient evidence for migration; trial source reverted to the pre-trial safe candidate. No implementation committed or pushed.

isolated_variants.experiment: experiments/83-trivial-copy-bench (allocator-api2 0.4.0 Vec with Global, one process, order rotated every repetition, 9 repetitions)
isolated_variants.note: Each case copies 65.5 million u64 values. At the default 256-element stride the raw copy takes about 11 ns per block and the fastest safe initialization about 87 ns.

overhead_cause_session_2026_10_17.cause: allocator-api2 0.4.0 implements Extend<T>, Extend<&T> (T: Copy) and resize_with as a per-element loop that compares len with capacity, writes one element and stores len back to the Vec on every iteration (vec/mod.rs lines 2808-2835 and 2894-2913). The disassembly of extend_copied and resize_with_first shows a scalar loop with one 8-byte store, a len store and a capacity reload per element, so LLVM does not vectorize it or turn it into memcpy. std::Vec avoids this with TrustedLen/Copy specialization, which a stable crate cannot use. The second copy_from_slice pass then adds a full memcpy. Debug assertions are not involved (release profile).
overhead_cause_session_2026_10_17.documentation_mismatch: allocator-api2 0.4.0 documents Extend<&T> as specialized to copy_from_slice for slice iterators, but the implementation is the same per-element loop; extend_ref was the slowest variant measured.

other_safe_paths_checked.Vec::extend_from_slice / extend_from_wit: call Clone (fails the custom-Clone bypass contract)
other_safe_paths_checked.Vec::append: Clone-free untyped memcpy, but needs a second AllocVec that already holds the copy, so it moves the problem
other_safe_paths_checked.Box<[T], A>::from(&[T]) for T: Copy then: Clone-free memcpy, but allocates a new exact-length buffer from A::default(): changes capacity (increment), allocation count and allocator selection
other_safe_paths_checked.spare_capacity_mut + <[MaybeUninit<T>]>:: safe single memcpy, but publishing the length needs unsafe set_len; allocator-api2 0.4.0 has no safe length publication
other_safe_paths_checked.bytemuck: requires Pod (no padding); cannot cover generic T: Copy
other_safe_paths_checked.newer allocator-api2: 0.4.0 is the latest published version (cargo info, 2026-10-17)

padding_contract_determination.decision: Padding preservation is not an exposed contract of the safe API.
evidence: Public docs (DynamicArray::from_copied_trivial, assign_trivial, DynamicArrayStorageExtension::copy_date_trivial) promise a bitwise copy that bypasses Clone; none promise padding bytes. Only the private copy_bits module doc says 'complete object representations'.
Safe Rust cannot read padding bytes; typed reads and writes leave padding unspecified, so no safe caller can observe it.

Only unsafe code reading through block_at/block_address can see bytes, and reading padding is defined only when the producer also wrote it as raw bytes. No crate, test, or fixture in the repository does this (grep for the trivial-copy entry points and raw block accessors, 2026-10-17).
padding_contract_determination.consequence: A one-pass value copy (extend copied) would satisfy the contract if the private module doc is corrected; ordinary value copying is not presented as padding preservation. The blocker is performance, not representation.
